questions.question: If the cost price of an item is $100 and it is sold for $120, what is the profit percentage?
questions.questionHtml: If the cost price of an item is $100 and it is sold for $120, what is the profit percentage?
questions.solution: Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price = $120 - $100 = $20. Profit Percentage = (Profit/Cost Price) × 100 = (20/100) × 100 = 20%
questions.subject: quantitative-aptitude

questions.question: A man sells an article at a loss of 10%. If he had sold it for $45 more, he would have gained 5%. Find the cost price.
questions.questionHtml: A man sells an article at a loss of 10%. If he had sold it for $45 more, he would have gained 5%. Find the cost price.
questions.solution: Let CP = x. At 10% loss, SP = 0.9x. At 5% gain, SP = 1.05x. Difference = 1.05x - 0.9x = 0.15x = $45. So x = $45/0.15 = $300.
questions.subject: quantitative-aptitude

questions.question: If the selling price of 10 articles is equal to the cost price of 12 articles, what is the profit percentage?
questions.questionHtml: If the selling price of 10 articles is equal to the cost price of 12 articles, what is the profit percentage?
questions.solution: Let CP of 1 article = 1. Then CP of 12 articles = 12. SP of 10 articles = 12, so SP of 1 article = 1.2. Profit = 1.2 - 1 = 0.2. Profit % = (0.2/1) × 100 = 20%
questions.subject: quantitative-aptitude

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 20% above cost price and allows a discount of 10%. Find his profit percentage.
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper marks his goods 20% above cost price and allows a discount of 10%. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution: Let CP = 100. Marked Price = 120. Discount = 10% of 120 = 12. SP = 120 - 12 = 108. Profit = 108 - 100 = 8. Profit % = 8%
